To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a digraph D is acyclic (resp., ordinary, unidirected) iff it is acyclic (ordinary, unidirected, respectively) after pushing a suitable subset of its vertices.

it is polynomial time solvable to decide whether a given multipartite digraph can be transformed into an acyclic digraph by pushing a subset of its vertices and, if so then, to find such a set of vertices.

a digraph D has the following property if and only if D is a multipartite tournament and does not contain a certain subdigraph: there exists a subset X ⊆ V(D) such that D can be made acyclical (resp. ordinary and unidirectional) by pushing X.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following questions: What is the computational complexity of the problem of deciding whether a digraph can be acyclic using the “push operation”?
the complexity of the following problem: given a digraph D, find the minimum cardinality subset of vertices X ⊆ V(D) such that D-X is acyclic (resp ordinary, unidirected) if such an X exists.
the following questions: Which digraphs can be made acyclical (resp. ordinary or unidirectional) by the push operation?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the push operation can be used to make a multipartite tournament ordinary if and only if the tournament is a disjoint union of cycles.
the problem of pushing the cycles out of a given digraph is solvable in linear time for the class of all multipartite tournaments. [1]
